To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

desensitisation of ATP-induced increases in [Ca2+], in human umbilical vein endothelial cells, occurs in the absence of protein kinase C, and that desensitised cells are not refractory to a second ATP challenge.

(1) ATP desensitizes its own effect on [Ca2+] and PGI2 release in human endothelium; (2) this is agonist-specific; (3) it is not blocked by staurosporine; (4) it is associated with uncoupling of P2Y receptors and phosphoinositidases C; (5) it is not associated with protein kinase C activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms involved in the regulation of prostacyclin (PGI2) release from human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC).
the role of the P2 purinoceptor in the regulation of the vascular endothelium.
the mechanisms by which human endothelial cells respond to extracellular ATP and other agonists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
desensitisation is not a function of PKC activation.
desensitisation of ATP mediated elevations in cytosolic calcium and prostacylin release in human endothelium cells does not involve PKC.
desensitisation of the P2 receptor in endothelium is not due to PKC activation, but that the P2 receptor is not desensitised in a classical manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the desensitization process is not a simple one, involving a number of different mechanisms, and that the desensitized response is dependent on the agonist used and the experimental conditions.
desensitizing ATP receptors do not involve PKC, but desensitizing histamine receptors do involve PKC.
desensitisation of the ATP-induced [Ca2+] response is not dependent on protein kinase C, and that this is reflected in the desensitisation response of prostacyclin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
desensitisation to ATP in human vascular endothelial cells is a phenomenon that is specific to the agonist, and that it is not due to the involvement of protein kinase C.
